newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS FED CATTLE SALES THIN AT $64 - FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS FED CATTLE SALES THIN AT $64 - FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales near midday Friday were light at $64.00 per cwt, down $2.00 from top prices last week, feedlot sources said.
About 5,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area and near 1,000 in Kansas, sources said.
At $64.00, fed cattle owners were losing an average of $20.00 per head and were reluctant to sell amid speculation that prices could improve next week, they said.
Most feedlots were fairly current, but will be carrying over cattle onto next week's showlists, some sources noted.
Outlooks for firm fed cattle prices next week were few but spurred by sentiment that beef prices may be near a near-term bottom following steep declines this week.
The lower prices encouraged brisk beef sales which several cattle feeders said they hope will continue next week. Brisk beef sales could translate to higher packer bids for cattle, they said.
However, early estimates for packer bids on Monday were $62.00 to $63.00 on projections for large cattle supplies, some sources said.
